subtitle: UPDATE Jul 31, 19:25 BRT, 65 days to the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). LULA BROKE THE SERIES TOP. The front-runner rose 1.00pp to 64.50% (vol USD 7.77M), passing for the first time the 63.50% the AFOS series had been matching without exceeding on Jul 26, 28, 30 and 31, and which had never been surpassed since Apr 14. Flávio ROSE 0.40pp, to 24.35% (vol USD 7.76M), and even so the gap WIDENED from +39.55pp to +40.15pp, the widest in the series that holds both names, which begins on May 3 and whose previous maximum was +39.80pp on Jul 26. It is the first reading above 40pp. THE DAY'S POLLING: Vox Brasil of Jul 31 (n=2,100, field Jul 26 to 28, margin of 2.15pp, 95% confidence, BR-01084/2026) gives Lula 40.5% x Flávio 31.2% in the first round, with Caiado 5.5%, Zema 3.2% and Renan Santos 3.0%, and Lula 47.5% x Flávio 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). That is a 9.3pp gap in the first round and 6.4pp in the runoff. THE POLITICAL FINDING IS FLÁVIO'S ISOLATION, and it has two parts on the same day. The PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election, saying it had consulted its state branches and decided not to call a National Convention, which blocks the ticket and rules out Tereza Cristina as running mate; the senator, who leads the PP in the Senate, shared the statement and complied, and Flávio replied that he respects it and does not give up. Hours later, Republicanos called a national convention for Aug 4 with the majority of the state branches consulted defending neutrality, heading toward a refusal of the alliance. The panel records the verb precisely: the PP DECIDED, Republicanos has NOT yet decided. On Jul 24 this series had already recorded that, without the União-PP federation, Flávio was seeking Republicanos and Podemos. The two doors he tried are now closing. THE SECOND FINDING IS RENAN SANTOS, and it is one of sequence. THREE consecutive institutes cut him: AtlasIntel 7.8% on Jul 29, PoderData 4% on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil 3.0% on Jul 31. With the price at 8.15% (vol USD 8.63M), the distance between market and poll reaches 5.15pp, the largest of the window. On Jul 29 the panel recorded that distance at 0.90pp and called it convergence. Three institutes later, it quadrupled, and it is on the record that the earlier reading did not hold. And there is a contradiction INSIDE the market itself: on the very day his winner contract gives up 0.30pp, the first-round second-place book RISES 3.25pp, from 6.10% to 9.35% (vol USD 1.09M). CAIADO GAVE BACK EVERYTHING AND MORE: he fell 0.95pp against the 2.55% of Jul 30 and returned to 1.60% (vol USD 5.22M), but ROSE 2.00pp in the third-place book, to 27.50%. On the same day, Vox gave him 5.5%, his best national reading of the window. CAMILO SANTANA rose 0.85pp, from 0.50% to 1.35% (vol USD 4.17M), and the series caveat is mandatory: 1.35% is NOT a record, his maximum is 4.10% from May 3, and the move is a recovery from the series MINIMUM, the 0.50% set on Jul 30. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 117.06M. Crossed with live Polymarket Jul 31, 22:25 UTC. A CAPTURE NOTE, and it explains the headline figure. The double-reading guard ran FOUR rounds today and failed all of them. The third failed precisely because Lula was in transit from 63.50% to 64.50%; the fourth repeated the entire presidential contract and failed a single book, the MDB in the Senate. That is why the presidential market goes in FIRM, including the 64.50%, and the MDB goes in as a declared RANGE of 24.65% to 26.65%.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: Polymarket 64.50% (up 1.00pp, vol USD 7.77M accumulated), 65 days to the election, BREAKING the top of the AFOS series. The gap over Flávio widens to +40.15pp, the widest since May 3 and the first above 40pp. The day's poll, Vox Brasil of Jul 31 (n=2,100, field Jul 26 to 28, margin of 2.15pp, 95% confidence, BR-01084/2026), gives 40.5% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 47.5% x 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno).
fortes: He PASSED for the first time the 63.50% he had been matching without breaking on Jul 26, 28, 30 and 31, and went to 64.50%, the highest value in the AFOS series since Apr 14.
Vox Brasil gives 47.5% x 41.1% in the runoff, and the 6.4pp fall OUTSIDE the two margins added together, so this reading does NOT describe a statistical tie.
Two of the week's three houses measure the first-round gap around 9pp, 9.1pp at AtlasIntel and 9.3pp at Vox, and the one that departs is PoderData, with 6pp.
The PCdoB formalized support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket, adding to the PSB, which made Alckmin the running mate official on Jul 29.
The institute records that, between May and July, Lula gained 7.3pp and Flávio lost 2.7pp within its own series, reversing a lead that had belonged to the senator.
fracos: The gap of +40.15pp is the widest since May 3, the start of the series that holds both names, but it widened on a day when Flávio ALSO rose, which rules out a reading of deterioration of the opponent.
The 40.5% at Vox in the first round remain below 50% plus one vote, meaning the reading describes a runoff and not a first-round win.
The Vox round did NOT publish approval or rejection, so the evaluation picture remains the one from Jul 30, with two houses pointing in opposite directions in the same week.
The 40.5% fall below the 44.9% AtlasIntel measured on Jul 29, and comparing different houses does not license calling that a decline.
The price did not react to any of the week's three national polls, which leaves the panel with no evidence that the market is reading them at all.
candidates.analise: His day ended where he had never been. The winner contract ROSE 1.00pp and went to 64.50%, breaking the 63.50% the series had been matching without exceeding on Jul 26, 28, 30 and 31. The gap WIDENED to +40.15pp, the widest since May 3 and the first above 40pp, and it widened even with Flávio rising 0.40pp, which means the move is demand for the front-runner and not deterioration of the opponent. THE POLL. Vox Brasil of Jul 31 (n=2,100, field Jul 26 to 28, margin of 2.15pp, 95% confidence, BR-01084/2026) gives 40.5% x 31.2% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 47.5% x 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The 6.4pp advantage in the runoff falls OUTSIDE the two margins added together, so this reading does not describe a statistical tie, unlike PoderData of Jul 30, which gave 3pp. And here is the record that organizes the week: THREE houses measured the first-round gap at 9.1pp (AtlasIntel, Jul 29), 6pp (PoderData, Jul 30) and 9.3pp (Vox, Jul 31). Two of them agree around 9pp and one is the outlier, and the outlier is PoderData. The panel records this without discarding any of them. The institute also reports that, between May and July, Lula grew 7.3pp and Flávio fell 2.7pp in its own series, reversing an advantage that had been the senator's; we reproduce this as a claim by the institute, because it is an internal comparison of theirs and we did not check the series. IN HIS CAMP, Camilo Santana rose 0.85pp and closed the capture at 1.35% and Geraldo Alckmin stayed at 0.45%, on the day the PCdoB formalized support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket. The panel records the coincidence and does not assert cause. On Camilo, the series caveat is mandatory: 1.35% is NOT a record of his, the series maximum is 4.10%, from May 3, and what happened was a recovery from the series MINIMUM, 0.50%, set on Jul 30. Both passed through higher values during the day, 2.20% and 1.10% at 17:33, and gave part of it back before this capture closed.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: Polymarket 24.35% (up 0.40pp, vol USD 7.76M accumulated), but the gap WIDENS to +40.15pp because Lula rose more. He FALLS in both placing books: 0.50pp in the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second place, to 78.50%, and stays at 5.65% in third place. Vox Brasil has him at 31.2% in the first round and 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). He lost the PP, and Republicanos is heading toward refusing an alliance.
fortes: RISES 0.40pp in the winner contract, to 24.35%, a fifth consecutive session without a fall in that contract.
His 41.1% in the Vox runoff sit 6.4pp from Lula, and it is his second best runoff mark in the window.

He announced on the morning of Jul 31 that Tereza Cristina had accepted the running-mate slot, but the PP declared neutrality minutes later and vetoed the ticket; he replied that he respects the decision and does not give up.
He holds 78.50% in the first-round second-place book, meaning the runoff position remains consolidated and not in dispute.
The PL rose 6.50pp in the Senate market, to 72.00%, the party's highest mark in that contract in the panel's tracking.
fracos: He ROSE in the winner contract and even so SAW THE GAP WIDEN from +39.55pp to +40.15pp, because Lula rose 1.00pp in the same session.
The PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election just minutes after his announcement, vetoing the ticket, and the senator publicly complied with the party decision.
The PP leadership assesses that she accepted the invitation precisely because she knew the party would block the ticket, a reading the same day's outcome made plausible.

Republicanos called a national convention for Aug 4 with the majority of the branches consulted defending neutrality, heading toward a refusal of the alliance; it is the second party to close the door in 24 hours, after the PP.
He still has NO running mate effectively settled, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away.
candidates.analise: His signal today is crossed and worth recording as such, without resolving it. He RISES 0.40pp in the winner contract, to 24.35%, and even so SEES THE GAP WIDEN, from +39.55pp to +40.15pp, because Lula rose 1.00pp in the same session. At the same time he FALLS 0.50pp in the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book, to 78.50% (vol USD 216,000), and stays at 5.65% in the third-place book. Rising in the chance of winning while giving ground on placing is an unusual combination. The counterpart to the fall in the second-place book is Renan Santos rising 3.25pp in that same contract, which suggests internal reallocation of that book rather than a fresh reading on who reaches the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). IN THE POLLING, Vox has him at 31.2% in the first round and 41.1% in the runoff, and the 6.4pp separating him from Lula fall outside the two margins added together, which moves away from the statistical-tie reading PoderData supported the previous day. HIS POLITICAL DAY WAS ONE OF DOORS CLOSING, and there were two. The PP VETOED it, and the case closed on the same day. On the morning of Jul 31, Flávio Bolsonaro said Tereza Cristina had accepted the running-mate invitation the night before, with the caveat that talks continued to see whether the party would move forward. Minutes later, the PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election, saying it had consulted its state branches and decided not to call a National Convention, which blocks the ticket. The senator, who leads the PP in the Senate, shared the party statement and complied. Flávio replied that he respects it and that he does not give up. And it was not only the PP. Hours later, Republicanos called a national convention for Aug 4 with the majority of the state branches consulted defending neutrality, heading toward a refusal of a national alliance with the senator. The panel separates the two verbs because they are not the same: the PP DECIDED, Republicanos has NOT yet decided. On Jul 24 this series recorded that, without the União-PP federation, Flávio was seeking Republicanos and Podemos; the two doors he tried that day are now closing. The Aug 5 deadline still has the running mate undefined. In the market, Tereza Cristina appears at 0.20% in the PRESIDENTIAL contract, and the distinction matters: that contract measures who wins the presidency, not who fills the running-mate slot.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: Polymarket 8.15% in the winner book (down 0.30pp, vol USD 8.63M accumulated). THREE consecutive institutes cut him, from 7.8% to 4% and now 3.0% at Vox, and the distance between price and polling reaches 5.15pp, the widest in the window. But the first-round second-place book RISES 3.25pp, to 9.35%, contradicting the polling on the same day.
fortes: RISES 3.25pp in the first-round second-place book, to 9.35%, recovering two thirds of what he had lost the previous day.
He stays at 61.50% in the first-round third-place book, keeping a cushion over Caiado, who rose to 27.50%.
Holds the largest accumulated volume among the competitive names in the presidential market, USD 8.63M, above Lula and Flávio.
Still holds the third-highest price in the presidential book, ahead of the entire chasing pack.
fracos: THREE consecutive institutes cut him: 7.8% at AtlasIntel of Jul 29, 4% at PoderData of Jul 30 and 3.0% at Vox of Jul 31.
The distance between price and polling reaches 5.15pp, the widest in the window, against the 0.90pp this panel recorded on Jul 29 and called convergence.
The three most recent readings are also the three lowest in the window, which describes a downward trend and not a spread between houses.
FALLS 0.30pp in the winner contract, to 8.15%, a fourth consecutive session of decline in that contract.
The market contradicted itself in his case within 24 hours, which weakens any reading of a stable repricing.
candidates.analise: This is the entry of the day and it has two parts pointing in opposite directions. THE FIRST is the polling, and it is a sequence, not an isolated figure. THREE consecutive institutes cut Renan Santos: AtlasIntel 7.8% on Jul 29, PoderData 4% on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil 3.0% on Jul 31. With the price at 8.15%, the distance between market and poll reaches 5.15pp, the largest of the window. On Jul 29 this panel wrote that the distance had fallen to 0.90pp and called that convergence, underlining that the narrowing was coming from the polling side. Three institutes later, the distance quadrupled. It is on the record that the Jul 29 reading did not hold, and that what the panel had been calling dispersion turned into something else: the three most recent readings are also the three lowest of the window, which describes a downward trend and not noise between houses. THE SECOND part is the market, and it contradicted itself. In the winner contract he gave up 0.30pp, to 8.15%. In the [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second-place book, however, he ROSE 3.25pp, from 6.10% to 9.35% (vol USD 1.09M), recovering two thirds of what he had lost 24 hours earlier. And he stayed at 61.50% in third place (vol USD 164,000). On Jul 30 the panel wrote that the money had reclassified him, taking away his [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) chance and pinning him in third. Today the same money gave much of that chance back, on the day the polling cut him for the third consecutive time. The panel records both directions and does not arbitrate which is right, because it has no way to. He holds the largest accumulated volume among the competitive names in the presidential market, USD 8.63M, above Lula and above Flávio.

Caiado gave back in one session the gain of two days on the very day he received the best polling of the window. Camilo Santana and Alckmin rose together, on the day of the PCdoB's formal support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket. caiado.label: CAIADO (PSD), presidential Poly 1.60% (down 0.95pp, vol USD 5.22M) | [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) third place 27.50% (up 2.00pp, vol USD 37,000) | second place 0.90% | candidate made official on Jul 26, with Kassab as running mate | latest national: Vox Brasil Jul 31, first round 5.5%
caiado.fortes: The day's poll is his BEST national reading of the window. Vox Brasil gives him 5.5% in the first round, above PoderData's 5% on Jul 30 and well above AtlasIntel's 3.1% on Jul 29. And the first-round third-place book followed: it RISES 2.00pp, to 27.50%, his highest mark in that contract in the panel's tracking. The divergence between institutes about him remains open at FOUR levels within the same month, 6% at Nexus, 5.5% at Vox, 5% at PoderData and 3.1% at AtlasIntel, and today's reading is the highest of the four.
caiado.fracos: The winner contract FELL 0.95pp, to 1.60%, and gave back in a single session the entire gain accumulated over two days. The series caveat is mandatory and it cuts both ways: 1.60% is his lowest value since Jul 22 and sits BELOW the 1.80% to 2.40% band in which he traded over that period, but it remains well above the series minimum, 0.90%, from Jul 9. The 2.55% of Jul 30 was an upward deviation, and the price gave that deviation back and also lost its recent floor. What remains is the reading that the market reallocated him from candidate to win to candidate to finish third, rising in the placing book and falling in the winner book, and that the polling did not follow that reallocation: it gave him precisely today the best mark of the window.

haddad.label: HADDAD (PT), presidential Poly 0.25% (up 0.10pp) | [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) second place 1.00% | not tested by Vox Brasil in any scenario, because he is running for the São Paulo state government
haddad.fortes: RISES 0.10pp in the winner contract, to 0.25%, and goes to 1.00% in the first-round second-place book. It is the second consecutive session of gains in the placing book.
haddad.fracos: Vox Brasil does not test him in any scenario, neither first round nor runoff, so he has no new polling in this round, and the absence of a test in a national poll is information the panel records rather than repeating the previous day's figure as if it were new. The interpretive caveat stands and needs saying plainly: he is NOT a presidential candidate, he is running for governor of São Paulo, and the scenario that favours him in the polls is a hypothesis and not a candidacy in progress. At a price of 0.30%, a 0.15pp rise carries almost no information.

zema.label: ZEMA (Novo), presidential Poly 0.35% (down 0.20pp, vol USD 4.59M) | [first-round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) third place 4.45% | Vox Brasil Jul 31: first round 3.2% | made official by Novo on Jul 27, still WITHOUT a running mate, deadline Aug 5
zema.fortes: In the polling he is stable: Vox's 3.2% are essentially the same 3% as PoderData of Jul 30 and above AtlasIntel's 2.8% of Jul 29. He holds 4.45% in the first-round third-place book, ahead of the whole chasing pack except Caiado, and has been official for Novo since Jul 27.

And the day was bad on the party front: Marcelo Aro left his Senate ticket to run for the state government of Minas Gerais, a move Zema publicly called betrayal, and Novo ruled out Barbosa as running mate, heading toward an all-Novo ticket. He remains WITHOUT a defined running mate, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away. A series caveat, and it is a large one: his maximum in the AFOS series is 10.10%, from Apr 26, so 0.35% is less than a twentieth of that level and moves of 0.20pp in that range carry almost no informational value.

quadroComparativo.s: The judicial axis produced plenty of fact today, but none of it points to the removal of a justice: the investigations target a senator and a private individual, not a member of the Court. With USD 83,000 of accumulated volume against USD 117.06M in the presidential market, a flat price in the face of facts that do not touch the object of the contract is the expected behavior.

cruzamento: THE CROSS-READING OF JUL 31 ended with the front-runner where he had never been. Lula ROSE 1.00pp and went to 64.50% (vol USD 7.77M), passing for the first time since Apr 14 the 63.50% the AFOS series had been matching without exceeding on Jul 26, 28, 30 and 31. Flávio ROSE 0.40pp, to 24.35% (vol USD 7.76M), and even so the gap WIDENED from +39.55pp to +40.15pp, the widest in the series that holds both names, which begins on May 3 and whose previous maximum was +39.80pp on Jul 26. It is the first reading above 40pp. The distinction matters and the panel makes it: the gap widened with the opponent ALSO rising, which describes demand for the front-runner and not deterioration on the other side. THE POLL. Vox Brasil of Jul 31 (n=2,100, field Jul 26 to 28, margin of 2.15pp, 95% confidence, BR-01084/2026) gives Lula 40.5% x Flávio 31.2% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), with Caiado 5.5%, Zema 3.2% and Renan Santos 3.0%, and Lula 47.5% x Flávio 41.1% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno). The 6.4pp advantage in the runoff falls OUTSIDE the two margins added together, so this reading does NOT describe a statistical tie, unlike PoderData of Jul 30. And the record that organizes the week is this: THREE houses measured the first-round gap at 9.1pp, 6pp and 9.3pp. Two agree around 9pp and the outlier is PoderData. On Jul 30 the panel wrote, correctly, that comparing different houses and calling the difference movement is swapping rulers; today's Vox reinforces that discipline by another route, showing that PoderData was the one outside the set. THE MARKET FINDING IS RENAN SANTOS, and it is one of sequence, not of an isolated figure. THREE consecutive institutes cut him: AtlasIntel 7.8% on Jul 29, PoderData 4% on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil 3.0% on Jul 31. With the price at 8.15% (vol USD 8.63M), the distance between market and poll reaches 5.15pp, the largest of the window. On Jul 29 this panel recorded that same distance at 0.90pp and called it convergence, underlining that it was narrowing from the polling side. Three institutes later, it quadrupled, and it is on the record that the earlier reading did not hold. And there is a contradiction INSIDE the market itself: on the very day the polling cuts him for the third time, the first-round second-place book RISES 3.25pp, from 6.10% to 9.35% (vol USD 1.09M), giving back two thirds of what had been taken the day before, while third place stays at 61.50%. On Jul 30 the panel wrote that the money had reclassified him; today the same money undid part of that. Both directions are recorded and neither is arbitrated. CAIADO GAVE BACK MORE THAN HE HAD GAINED: he fell 0.95pp against the 2.55% of Jul 30 and went to 1.60% (vol USD 5.22M), and at the same time ROSE 2.00pp in third place, to 27.50%. The series caveat cuts both ways and is necessary: 1.60% is his lowest value since Jul 22 and sits BELOW the 1.80% to 2.40% band in which he traded over that period, but it remains well above the series minimum, 0.90%, from Jul 9. On the same day, Vox gave him 5.5%, his best national reading of the window, and the divergence between institutes about him remains open at FOUR levels within the same month: 6%, 5.5%, 5% and 3.1%. CAMILO SANTANA rose 0.85pp, from 0.50% to 1.35% (vol USD 4.17M), and Geraldo Alckmin stayed at 0.45% (vol USD 4.98M), on the day the PCdoB formalized support for the Lula-Alckmin ticket. The panel records the coincidence and does not assert cause. On Camilo, the series caveat is mandatory: 1.35% is NOT a record, his maximum is 4.10%, from May 3, and the move is a recovery from the series MINIMUM, 0.50%, set on Jul 30. Both passed through higher values during the day, 2.20% and 1.10% at 17:33, and gave part of it back before this capture. THE PARTY AXIS was the day's story, and it has TWO doors, not one. The PP VETOED it, and the case closed on the same day. On the morning of Jul 31, Flávio Bolsonaro said Tereza Cristina had accepted the running-mate invitation the night before, with the caveat that talks continued to see whether the party would move forward. Minutes later, the PP announced NEUTRALITY in the election, saying it had consulted its state branches and decided not to call a National Convention, which blocks the ticket. The senator, who leads the PP in the Senate, shared the party statement and complied. Flávio replied that he respects it and that he does not give up. And it was not only the PP. Hours later, Republicanos called a national convention for Aug 4 with the majority of the state branches consulted defending neutrality, heading toward a refusal of a national alliance with the senator. The panel separates the two verbs because they are not the same: the PP DECIDED, Republicanos has NOT yet decided. On Jul 24 this series recorded that, without the União-PP federation, Flávio was seeking Republicanos and Podemos; the two doors he tried that day are now closing. The Aug 5 deadline still has the running mate undefined. In the market, Tereza Cristina appears at 0.20% in the PRESIDENTIAL contract, and the distinction matters: that contract measures who wins the presidency, not who fills the running-mate slot. In Minas Gerais, Marcelo Aro left Zema's Senate ticket to run for the state government, a move Zema publicly called betrayal, and Novo ruled out Barbosa as running mate. THE JUDICIAL AXIS produced the largest volume of new fact in the Master case since the inquiry was opened, and the panel records that the reading published at 17:33, that the day had no new act, was wrong. André Mendonça lifted the secrecy of part of the investigation examining whether senator Jaques Wagner received improper advantage to act in favor of Banco Master's interests in the Senate. With the secrecy lifted, a Federal Police report became public identifying 74 calls between the senator and Augusto Lima, a former partner of the bank, between November 2023 and May 2025, adding up to more than five hours and thirty minutes of conversation across 555 days. In the same decision, Mendonça authorized the police to monitor the location of the senator's mobile phone, citing the risk of a leak of the operation. Novo asked for proceedings to be opened in the Senate Ethics Council and Wagner said he will prove his innocence. A day earlier, on Jul 30, the same justice had authorized an inquiry into influence peddling by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, with the Health Ministry and the Presidency; Lula said his son will have to prove his innocence and that he will not use his office to protect him. None of this is a conviction and the panel does not treat it as such: these are an inquiry, a lifting of secrecy and a party petition. IN THE OTHER MARKETS, impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice was FLAT at 3.10% (vol USD 83,000), with no variation across the eight readings of the four guard rounds. It is worth underlining that this contract does NOT price the Wagner case, which runs against a senator and not against a justice, so a flat price there is not the market's answer to what came out today. In the Senate, the PL ROSE 6.50pp, to 72.00% (vol USD 258,000), and the MDB goes in as a declared RANGE of 24.65% to 26.65%: added together, the two carry more than 97% of the probability assigned to just two parties, which by itself indicates a wide spread. In inflation, the modal band remains 5.00% to 5.49%, at 38.30%, and the 4.50% to 4.99% band rose 1.20pp, to 33.70%, in a book of USD 81,000 not covered by the guard. A CAPTURE NOTE, and it explains the headline figure. The double-reading guard ran FOUR rounds today and failed all of them. The third failed precisely because Lula was in transit from 63.50% to 64.50%; the fourth repeated the entire presidential contract and failed a single book, the MDB in the Senate. That is why the presidential market goes in FIRM, including the 64.50%, and the MDB goes in as a declared RANGE. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 117.06M.
